E065-01.notes: Two independent clauses. A comma splice; B fused run-on; D semicolon plus 'and' is nonstandard/redundant joining on ACT. C makes two sentences correctly.

E065-02.notes: Paragraph is about rescues; A bridges from rowing skill (P1) to rescues. B harbor traffic, C siblings' schooling, D routine keeper chores are all off-topic for the rescue paragraph.

E065-03.notes: Sentence 6 moves forward in time from the 1858 rescue. B 'Before then' reverses chronology; C no contrast exists; D sentence 6 is not an example of the single 1858 rescue but a continuation.

E065-04.notes: Concision. A 'severe and violent' redundant/wordy; C 'violently severe' awkward and redundant; D 'severity so severe' redundant. B 'storms so severe that' is concise and grammatical.

E065-05.notes: Phrase shows urgency/speed. A no such info earlier; B it says nothing about why the boat overturned; C essay focuses on Ida, not the lighthouse, and the detail supports that focus.

E065-06.notes: Nonessential appositive needs commas on both sides. A missing opening comma; B missing closing comma; D no commas.

E065-07.notes: Inverted sentence; subject is singular 'President Ulysses S. Grant', so 'was'. A plural trap triggered by 'them'; C plural and wrong tense; D 'being' makes a fragment.

E065-08.notes: Register. A, B, C are colloquial ('make a big deal', 'couldn't have cared less', 'wasn't all that into'); D matches the essay's formal tone.

E065-09.notes: 'a position she held...' is an appositive modifying the appointment; comma correct. B semicolon followed by a fragment; C creates a fragment; D misplaced comma garbles meaning ('herself a position').

E065-10.notes: Essay is a biographical account of Ida Lewis's rescues and fame. A essay mentions keeping the lamp lit but gives no detail on how; C says only when she was appointed, nothing general about appointment practice; D false, it mentions duties like keeping the lamp burning.
